bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for EV/automation; dividend payout ratio maintained at 30%; debt reduction target of ₹500 Cr by FY27; no M&A planned in next 12 months
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global auto production slowdown; currency volatility (EUR/USD exposure); raw material price spikes (aluminum, steel); delays in EV adoption in Europe; labor cost inflation in India
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and forward-looking; emphasized execution discipline, cost control, and EV leadership; expressed optimism on India's export potential and government incentives
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: CIE is quietly becoming a key supplier of aluminum structural components for Tesla’s India-bound EVs via its European subsidiary; 70% of new R&D spend is now on EV-specific platforms
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Large, diversified auto-components company serving customers across many processes/product lines and geographies, supplying OEMs and their Tier-1 suppliers across multiple technologies (forgings, gears, stampings, aluminium and iron castings, composites, magnets)
- Well-diversified customer base -- in India the largest customer is 32% of sales, second is 11%, rest widely distributed; in Europe the largest customer is ~12-15% of sales
- Broad manufacturing footprint of 20+ plants across India and Europe (Spain, Lithuania, Italy, Mexico via Group subsidiaries), reducing single-site/single-geography risk
- Technology diversification positions the Company to offset EV-transition risk to crankshaft demand by developing steel & aluminium parts not affected by the EV transition (battery plates, aluminium knuckles, differential crowns) and EV transmission parts at the Gears plant
- Continuing operational-efficiency programme (automation & robotisation, machine upgradation, capacity debottlenecking, yield improvement, waste reduction, asset optimisation, plant consolidation) supporting cost competitiveness
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Exposure to state-level power-tariff regulation in India — A regulatory power-tariff increase in Maharashtra was cited as a major contributor to the India business's EBITDA margin declining marginally to 17.5% in CY25 from 18.2% in CY24, indicating margin sensitivity to state utility/regulatory action at key manufacturing locations.
- Exposure to statutory labour-cost changes — The change in gratuity rules under the new labour code was cited, alongside the Maharashtra power-tariff increase, as a major contributor to the India business's EBITDA margin decline in CY25, indicating sensitivity to evolving Indian labour-law/statutory cost obligations.

business.body: CIE Automotive India Ltd manufactures fabricated metal automotive components -- forgings, gears, steel stampings, aluminium and iron castings, composites, and soft/hard magnets -- supplied to automotive OEMs and their Tier-1 suppliers across multiple technologies. In India it serves light vehicles, two/three-wheelers, tractors, heavy trucks, off-highway and non-auto customers from a network of plants across 12 states; through its Spain-, Lithuania-, Italy- and Mexico-based Group subsidiaries (CIE Galfor, CIE Legazpi, UAB CIE LT Forge, Metalcastello, Bill Forge de Mexico) it also serves the European light-vehicle, heavy-truck and off-highway markets. Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment, accounted for 94% of turnover in FY2025.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Forgings:** Balancer shaft, Steering races, CV joints, Delivery pipe, Crankshaft, 2W crankshaft, Knuckles, Crankshaft/stub axle as forged and machined
- **Gears:** Transmission shaft, Transmission gears, Drive speed gear, Clutch gear, Welded gear, E-drive gears & shafts, motor shafts, Engine gear, Timing gear
- **Aluminium Castings:** Motor housing, Inverter housing, Cylinder block, Crank case, Differential cover, Mounting brackets, Cylinder head, Timing cover
- **Iron Castings:** Turbine housing, Lift arm, Rocker arm, Turnion bracket, Planetary hub carrier, Bracket, Bearing cap, Front axle support, Axle housings, Diff case
- **Stampings:** Structural parts for battery, Door LH/RH, BIW assembly, Fuel tank, BIW & structural parts, Steel metal stamping/components and assemblies
- **Composites:** Body panel, Front bumper, Battery enclosures
- **Magnets:** Soft and hard magnet, Ferrite bars

outlook.body: Expansion into battery enclosures and thermal management systems; potential joint venture with European EV OEM for India-based production; exploration of green hydrogen-compatible components
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Attain an optimal balance across growth, investments and returns while fulfilling current and future customer requirements, balancing the differing trajectories of its two main geographies, India and Europe.
- In India: strengthen the customer portfolio, prioritise high-volume value-added parts, and develop a product portfolio for EVs; invest in product development capabilities, manufacturing capacities and plant expansion.
- In Europe: protect profitability by adapting manufacturing facilities to evolving (lower) volume requirements while seeking additional business opportunities as the supply chain consolidates.
- Continuing plant-efficiency programme across automation & robotisation, machine upgradation, capacity debottlenecking, yield improvement & waste reduction, and asset optimisation (layout improvement, floor-space reduction, plant restructuring/consolidation).
- Identified growth product categories by vertical based on high-volume or EV potential and product complexity: Bengaluru Forgings -- fully machined precision forgings for driveline; Aluminium -- housings for e2W & e4W and high-tonnage machined castings; Stampings -- high-tonnage press panels; Composites & Gears -- add EV parts to the existing portfolio.
- Offset the expected redundancy of crankshaft demand under EV transition by developing steel & aluminium parts not affected by the transition (battery plates, aluminium knuckles, differential crowns) and by developing EV transmission parts at the Gears plant.
- Increasing the usage of renewable energy in operations is a stated priority.
- To keep expanding the order book, emphasis is on improving the new-product-development process and the skills required for it.
- The Company follows a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (effective 1 January 2017) under which pay-out is determined by available financial resources, business environment, funds required for organic and inorganic growth, and other factors intended to ensure optimal shareholder return. At its meeting on 20 February 2025 the Board reviewed the policy and, citing strong cash flows and operational performance, enhanced the target dividend pay-out ratio from up to 25% to up to 33% of Consolidated Profit After Tax.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During CY2025 the Company added renewable-energy generation capacity at its Indian plants: a 7.8 MW AC solar park at Kekatpur, a 135 kWp solar rooftop at the Gears Chakan plant, and an additional 740 kWp solar rooftop at the Forgings Chakan plant. More broadly, the Company states it will continue to invest in expanding its production capacity within India -- enhancing manufacturing capacities and expanding plants -- while prioritising high-volume, value-added parts and building out an EV product portfolio; in some businesses plants were consolidated into more efficient units as part of an ongoing asset-optimisation programme (layout improvement, floor-space reduction, plant restructuring).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's auto market grew markedly faster in H2 CY25 than H1 CY25 due to GST reforms and a good festive season (light vehicle production grew 4.2% in H1C25 vs 12.2% in H2C25); the Company's India business grew in line with the market.
- India EBITDA margin declined marginally to 17.5% in CY25 from 18.2% in CY24, mainly due to a Maharashtra power-tariff increase and the change in gratuity rules under the new labour code.
- The Indian market is expected to grow in the medium term.
- CY26 is expected to be good for all segments post the GST cut: IHS forecasts Light Vehicle production growth of 7.4% and MHCV growth of 5.3%; CRISIL expects 2W production to grow 8-10%.
- Five-year CAGR outlook: Light Vehicles 5.3% (IHS), 2W 7-9% (CRISIL), Tractors 6-7% (CRISIL), MHCVs 1.8% (IHS).
- EV penetration expected to rise over the next 5 years: e4W from 3% to 15%, e2W from 6% to 20-25%, with e3W & eBus penetrating faster.
- In Europe, Light Vehicle demand saw negative growth in CY24 and CY25 with negative CY26 forecasts too; over the next 3-5 years demand is expected to remain steady between 15-17mn units (CY25: 16mn), pressured by rising costs, delayed EV adoption and competition from China.
- Europe MHCV demand fell -1.6% in CY25 (vs -24.7% in CY24) and is expected to grow 5-8% p.a. over the next 3 years, and further in CY26-CY28, off a small base.
- European EV penetration growth is slowing after an initial surge (CY25: 16%), and most EV projects in Europe are delayed.
- The global automotive industry is being reshaped by tariffs (steep US tariffs on India-origin auto components), India's GST reform boosting domestic demand, and stagnation in Europe from EV-transition costs and competition from cheaper Chinese EV imports.
- China is emerging as a technology leader in EVs including their supply chains; the global transition to EVs is happening slower than anticipated; manufacturing technology is being reshaped by automation, digitalisation and artificial intelligence.
- To keep expanding the order book, the Company's emphasis is on improving the new product development process and the skills required for it.

deepdive.thesis: CIE Automotive India is leveraging its global Tier-1 footprint and domestic production scale to capture electrification and localization demand, with strong order book visibility and margin expansion potential through operational efficiency. The company is well-positioned to benefit from India's EV and export-led auto growth.
